t.1.40.1: The bard said: Seeing him thus encircled by the coils of the serpent, all the ministers, their faces pale, wept, deeply grieved.
t.1.40.2: Then, hearing that cry, the ministers fled, and they saw the wondrous serpent going through the sky.
t.1.40.3: Deeply overwhelmed with grief, they beheld Takṣaka, the best of serpents, radiant as a lotus, as he seemed to draw a parting line across the sky.
t.1.40.5: Then, when the king had been slain by the fiery venom of Takṣaka, the pure twice-born royal priest performed all the rites for the next world, and so too did those ministers of that king.
t.1.40.4: Then, out of fear, they abandoned that house, enveloped by fire and blazing with the flames born of the poison from the serpent, and fled in all directions; and the house fell as if struck by a thunderbolt.
t.1.40.6: All the people dwelling in the city came together and made his son, still a child, their king, the slayer of enemies, the foremost hero of the Kurus, whom the people call King Janamejaya.
t.1.40.7: Then that best of kings, noble-minded though still a mere boy, the eldest-born of the bulls among the Kurus, ruled the kingdom together with those same ministers and family priests, just as his heroic great-grandfather had done.
t.1.40.9: Then the king, having examined the matter in accordance with dharma, gave Vapuṣṭamā to the foremost hero of the Kurus. And he, having obtained her, was filled with joy, and never set his mind on other women.
t.1.40.8: Then the ministers of that ruler, having looked upon their king, the scorcher of foes, approached Suvarṇavarman, the lord of Kāśi, and sought Vapuṣṭamā in marriage for him.
t.1.40.11: And Vapuṣṭamā too, having then obtained that excellent husband, a king of renowned beauty, that lovely woman, the beauty of the inner apartments, delighted him with heartfelt affection in their times of pleasure.
t.1.40.10: Among blossoming lakes and woods the mighty one, his heart serene, took his pleasure; that best of princes delighted himself just as Purūravas did of old after winning Urvaśī.
